themes_detail.label: Street Vendor Crackdown Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 72 THIS WEEK, up 317% from the 17.2-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.63), signaling either a new enforcement sweep or emerging vendor-related disorder in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights.
evidence: 72 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 17.2 weekly average (4-week baseline), z-score 4.63
Vendor Enforcement in top 10 complaints overall (362 total complaints in 90-day period)
No prior news or community board discussion of vendor issues, suggesting sudden change
reporting_angles: Is NYPD or DOC launching a new enforcement initiative? Interview enforcement agencies about strategy.
Talk to street vendors and small business advocates about impact on livelihoods and whether complaints are justified or over-policing.

themes_detail.label: Construction Lead Dust Alert
themes_detail.summary: Lead dust complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, up 540% from the 0.6-per-week baseline (z-score: 4.85), a critical public health signal in a neighborhood with dense historic housing stock and families with young children.
evidence: 4 construction lead dust complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average, z-score 4.85
1,203 DOB building permits filed in past 90 days (868 alterations), indicating heavy renovation activity
Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights have high concentration of pre-1978 housing (lead paint risk), especially among vulnerable populations
reporting_angles: Cross-reference the 4 lead complaints with specific DOB permits filed this week to identify which projects lack proper lead-safe practices.
Interview NYC Health Department and HPD about enforcement of lead-safe renovation standards; talk to parents and pediatricians about screening rates.

themes_detail.label: Park Safety & Animal Concerns Spike
themes_detail.summary: Two related spikes emerged last week: Violation of Park Rules complaints (3 last week, up 2300% from 0.1 baseline) and Animal in a Park complaints (8 last week, up 357% from 1.8 baseline), suggesting either a wildlife incursion or enforcement response in district parks.
evidence: Violation of Park Rules: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average, z-score 8.69 (2300% increase)
Animal in a Park: 8 complaints last week vs. 1.8 weekly average, z-score 5.74 (357% increase)
Community board repeatedly requests new equipment for Parks maintenance, suggesting chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks to determine if a specific incident (e.g., coyote sighting, rat infestation) triggered complaints in Fort Greene Park or Brooklyn Bridge Park.
Interview park users and community members about safety concerns and whether park conditions are deteriorating.

themes_detail.label: Real-Time Enforcement Initiative
themes_detail.summary: Real-time enforcement complaints surged to 8 LAST WEEK, up 1500% from the 0.5-per-week baseline (z-score: 10.61, highest spike in dataset), likely signaling a new city enforcement operation or pilot program in the district.
evidence: 8 real-time enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly baseline, z-score 10.61 (highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
No prior complaints of this type in historical record, indicating entirely new phenomenon
No news coverage or community board discussion suggests this may be unreported city initiative
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with NYC agencies to determine what 'real-time enforcement' operation was launched in CD 302.
Interview 311 complaint filers to understand what they were reporting and whether it reflects genuine new enforcement or citizen confusion about a city program.

themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Rising
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints jumped to 6 LAST WEEK, up 500% from the 1.0-per-week baseline (z-score: 5.77), coinciding with 1,203 permits filed in 90 days and three active ULURP rezoning proposals, suggesting construction compliance issues amid development surge.
evidence: Building/Use complaints: 6 last week vs. 1.0 weekly average, z-score 5.77 (500% increase)
1,203 DOB permits filed in past 90 days, 868 are alterations—high activity period for violations
Three active ULURP applications (395 Flatbush, Columbia Heights rezoning) indicate neighborhood under development pressure
reporting_angles: Request DOB violation data for CD 302 in past 4 weeks; identify which properties are repeat offenders or under rezoning proposals.
Interview DOB and community board about whether enforcement resources are adequate to monitor the current construction surge.
